applies_why: The judge labels Matthew 1:20 UNDERDETERMINED while also saying the verse's own words state the source, so the rule about single-verse openness and two meanings applies.
quote: D2 vs C1 (Matthew 1:20): UNDERDETERMINED -- the challenger's covenant-origin analogy is footed (1 Chronicles 28:6, Acts 1:8) but the sentence's own words state the source of what is in the womb; answered in [CR3] LINK 2.
rule_words: That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. When one verse's words carry two meanings at once, both stand; the verse is not open.
room: I interpreted 'When one verse's words carry two meanings at once, both stand; the verse is not open': one reading is that this bars UNDERDETERMINED whenever the verse itself supplies the meanings; the other is that UNDERDETERMINED may be used whenever a verse can be read two ways.
why: The judge calls the matter UNDERDETERMINED even though it says Matthew 1:20's own words state the source, so K-S2 requires both meanings to stand rather than treating the verse as open.
